nodes.description: This journey is one of two proofs holding the proven rung. The assertion is sensitive to how many settled claims cite src/fsglob.rs, so settling unrelated groundings can break it without any checkpoint regression. body.evidence: journeys/surfaces/semantic-commit-recommendation.surface.json:503-541 — setup operation verify-isolated-checkpoint-fixture runs `loom sync --json` and asserts /edges_staled==0, /validations_reset==0, /files_changed==0; setup.git declares dirty_paths ["src/fsglob.rs"] (:544-550). Observed this session: the fixture failed first on validations_reset=1 (while journey:release-workflow:proof was blocked), then after that cleared, on edges_staled=1 with files_changed=0. Three reproductions in copied graphs — plain sync; sync with a dirtied src/fsglob.rs; and a full replay of the setup ops (validation remove x2, validation add, validation run, then sync) — all returned edges_staled=0, so the staling edge cannot be identified from outside the journey runtime. A dirtied src/fsglob.rs alone stales ace00d914d (validates: contract: root-confined paths to Root-confined paths, evidence `cargo test --lib fsglob::tests`), which the fixture normally isolates by removing that validation.
body.impact: This journey is one of two proofs holding the proven rung. nodes.name: intent 'grade liveness-only proofs' has clause(s) grounded by no implements edge (sole grounding is src/proofstrength.rs)
nodes.description: The intent is a conjunction but src/proofstrength.rs is its only implements edge, so any clause realized elsewhere in the tree is unproven and invisible to the coverage gate. body.evidence: ADVERSARIAL READER CLAIM, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The cited spans are accurate (src/proofstrength.rs:262-297 reported_assertions; 1522-1539 ran_and_passed/S0 early-return; 1547-1554 S1 assignment when observed_assertions is None), but the grading intent this edge claims to ground -- 'a successful observed run with zero assertions grades exactly S1, a blocked/unrunnable proof grades S0' -- is not realized by `reported_assertions` at all. `reported_assertions` (262-297) is a pure helper that returns Option<String> counting/parsing assertion evidence; it contains no Strength/S0/S1 logic whatsoever. The actual grading decisions (the S0 early-returns at 1511 and 1533-1539, and the S1 assignment at 1548-1554) live in a *different* function, `pub fn grade` (defined at line 1495), which merely calls reported_assertions as one input. The edge's locator is 'reported_assertions' only (no `grade` in the `;`-separated list), so the grounding is misplaced onto a helper that does not itself grade anything; the intent's truth lives in `grade()`.
body.impact: The intent is a conjunction but src/proofstrength.rs is its only implements edge, so any clause realized elsewhere in the tree is unproven and invisible to the coverage gate. Triage should confirm which clause is uncovered and add the missing grounding edge rather than re-verdict the existing one.

nodes.description: If the claim holds, the implements edge 3da0c50a is not grounded as asserted and should be re-verdicted. body.evidence: ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER CLAIM, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY THE RECORDING AGENT. src/signal.rs doctor() (937-1150, function span confirmed exact) contains a silent failure path the evidence doesn't cite and that contradicts the universal claim 'reports every detected graph-integrity violation ... without silently treating an invalid graph as clean.' At line 1127: `if let Ok(entries) = crate::federation::read_upstream_entries(store) { ... }` — the entire orphaned-upstream-intent check (1127-1145) is skipped whenever read_upstream_entries returns Err. Per src/federation.rs:36-41, that function returns Err specifically when the stored `upstream_graphs` meta value fails to parse as JSON (a malformed/corrupted graph state) — i.e. exactly a 'detected' anomaly. In that case doctor() neither reports a DoctorIssue nor propagates an error; it silently proceeds as if there were zero orphaned UpstreamIntent nodes, even though doctor's own comment at 1123-1126 calls that condition 'a hard integrity issue.' The proposed_evidence's own cited range for 'appending a DoctorIssue for every violation found (950-1121)' stops just short of this block (1127-1145), so the reviewer never examined the swallowed branch. This is a concrete carve-out where a detected malformed-input condition is silently treated as clean rather than reported.
body.impact: If the claim holds, the implements edge 3da0c50a is not grounded as asserted and should be re-verdicted. nodes.name: Journey semantic-commit-recommendation derivation semantic-commit-recommendation-v1
nodes.description: This projection separates the readiness decision, the recommendation projection, the autonomous checkpoint decision, and the Loom-truth boundary. It reuses the approved doctor behavior instead of duplicating graph-integrity diagnosis, and it keeps Loom's command read-only while letting the acting LLM decide whether a scoped Git checkpoint improves history.

human_decision.response: approved

items.text: Checkpoint readiness consumes the already approved deterministic doctor behavior; creating another doctor Intent would duplicate the same integrity criterion.
The conjunction of implementation, proof, synchronization, integrity, export, and semantic-cohesion evidence is one fail-closed decision with one observable ready-or-blocked result.
This is the user-facing read model produced from readiness evidence and is independently falsifiable from the gate that supplies that evidence.
The checkpoint should reduce human friction: Loom supplies evidence and exact scope, while the LLM exercises bounded judgment about whether a commit is useful and safe.
Local history checkpoints are reversible autonomous workflow, while publishing them changes shared external state and therefore remains a separate human authority decision.
Repository history can attest that a cohesive snapshot was chosen, but it cannot become a second authority for Loom's graph truth.

body.evidence: ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER CLAIM, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY THE RECORDING AGENT. Citations are accurate (src/signal.rs:360-407: by_command built 369-383, `if intents.len() < 2 { continue; }` at 387-388, Smell pushed 394-404). But the 'proves' map at src/signal.rs:362-367 is `BTreeMap<&str, &str>` keyed by validation id, built with `proves.insert(e.from_id.as_str(), e.to_id.as_str())` inside a loop over all Validates edges — this OVERWRITES per validation id, keeping only the last intent seen. A single Validation node with multiple Validates edges to distinct intents (a real, common pattern confirmed by src/checkpoint.rs:682 `store.edges_with(Some(EdgeKind::Validates), Some(&validation.id), None)` returning a Vec, and the function's own docstring example at signal.rs:343-355 describing exactly 'one command proves seven behaviors') collapses to a single intent in `proves`, so by_command never accumulates 2+ distinct intents for that node and the smell silently fails to fire for the exact scenario the docstring cites as the motivating bug. The code does not report all behaviors sharing a proof mechanism as claimed.
body.impact: If the claim holds, the implements edge 42dfe933 is not grounded as asserted and should be re-verdicted. Filed as a finding rather than a failing claim because the reviewer population was deliberately biased toward refutation and this specific counterexample was not confirmed by a second reader. Triage should confirm or dismiss against the cited spans before any verdict is recorded.

items.text: Checkpoint readiness consumes the already approved deterministic doctor behavior; creating another doctor Intent would duplicate the same integrity criterion.
The conjunction of implementation, proof, synchronization, integrity, export, and semantic-cohesion evidence is one fail-closed decision with one observable ready-or-blocked result.
This is the user-facing read model produced from readiness evidence and is independently falsifiable from the gate that supplies that evidence.
The checkpoint should reduce human friction: Loom supplies evidence and exact scope, while the LLM exercises bounded judgment about whether a commit is useful and safe.
Local history checkpoints are reversible autonomous workflow, while publishing them changes shared external state and therefore remains a separate human authority decision.
Repository history can attest that a cohesive snapshot was chosen, but it cannot become a second authority for Loom's graph truth.
The blocked outcome is what readiness produces when no single Intent bundle explains the change, and it must be observable as typed blockers rather than a partial scope.
The authored step expects a refusal or missing answer to leave the checkpoint local; that outcome is independently falsifiable from the gate that demands the decision.
The authored step expects ambiguous ownership to cause deferral rather than a guess; deferring is a distinct observable outcome from deciding to commit.

body.evidence: ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER CLAIM, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY THE RECORDING AGENT. Citations are literally accurate (src/callgraph.rs:396-461, 431-436 Caller resolution tagging, 450-453 exact count, 454-457 heuristic count, 458 `unresolved_calls: self.unresolved`), but the conclusion overreaches. `self.unresolved` (field defined at callgraph.rs:51, incremented at 97 and 101) is a GLOBAL count of unresolvable callee names accumulated once for the entire codebase during build() -- it is not scoped to `starts`/the target symbol at all. Every call to impact_from(), regardless of which target symbol is queried, copies the same self.unresolved value verbatim (line 458). Confirmed via the CLI surface at src/commands/diagnostics_cmd.rs:1219 (`unresolved_calls: cg.unresolved`) and the printed line at 1294 ('{unresolved} call(s) unresolved (std/third-party)') -- explicitly a whole-graph stat, unlike `exact`/`heuristic` which ARE derived from the target-specific `callers` list (diagnostics_cmd.rs:1190-1192). So `loom impact foo` and `loom impact bar` report identical unresolved_calls for two different targets. The intent_desc's claim that Loom reports 'exact callers, heuristic callers, and unresolved calls' all 'for a target symbol' as three parallel per-target resolution classes is false for the third: unresolved_calls is not a resolution class of the target's callers, it is an unrelated codebase-wide tally.

nodes.name: journey run/diagnose plain-text output drops the blocking reason: emit_report prints only status and assertion counts, so a blocked journey reports "0 passed, 0 failed" with no cause unless the operator knows to re-run with --json
nodes.description: A blocked journey is the case where the operator most needs the cause, and it is the one case the plain-text output withholds — 'blocked (0 passed, 0 failed)' reads like an empty or broken profile rather than one missing environment variable. It cost a real detour in a live migration before --json was tried. This got sharper in 1e52d53: the new cold-rehearsal refusal now explicitly routes operators to journey diagnose, so this output is the first wall a confused operator hits. The fix is small and additive — append detail to the human line when it is non-empty; the data is already in the report struct.

body.evidence: src/commands/journey/mod.rs:2391-2403 emit_report formats the human line as "Journey '{}:{}' {} ({} assertion(s) passed, {} failed)" from journey_id, profile, status, assertions_passed and assertions_failed only. RuntimeReport carries a detail field (:2371 detail: String) which is serialized into the JSON value passed to emit_runtime_value, but the plain-text branch never reads it. Reproduced on an external target repo (twoyoule): 'loom journey run 34ca2da0 --profile proof' and 'loom journey diagnose 34ca2da0 --profile proof' both printed exactly "Journey 'settle-platform-credits:proof' blocked (0 assertion(s) passed, 0 failed)" and nothing more; re-running with --json returned "detail": "declared operation environment variable 'TWOYOULE_CLI_BASE_URL' is missing", which is the whole answer.

nodes.name: Cold rehearsal cannot run outside loom's own repository layout
nodes.description: rehearse-cold is documented and briefed as the cheap, token-free pre-flight, so target repos are told to run it constantly and cannot. A fail-fast now names the limitation instead of leading callers through four escalating validator errors, but the capability itself is still loom-only. Generalizing it means a gitignore-aware snapshot walk (or manifest-declared ignore roots) and a graph-derived surface root, both of which move release-plane trust boundaries and need their own tests.

body.evidence: Four independent constraints, verified in source on 2026-08-15 and observed against a real target repo (twoyoule, 1104-entry inventory): SURFACE_MANIFEST_ROOT is the constant 'journeys/surfaces' (src/release.rs:42); validate_candidate_path rejects any path entering a reserved component at any depth (src/release.rs:4064+), and the eight components are a dev-machine profile (.claude, .qoder, .reasonix, ...); INVENTORY_SECRET_PATTERNS refuses '.env.*'; and validate_inventory_manifest bails with 'weakens the canonical reserved/secret policy' if a manifest tries to relax either list. Structurally, candidate_file_plan compares against 'git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard' while scan_snapshot_files walks the working tree with zero references to gitignore, so the two required file sets cannot agree for any repo with ignored artifacts outside those eight roots — twoyoule measured 35,361 such files plus 42 symlinks under node_modules/.bin. loom's own repo escapes only because its build output is confined to target/, which is reserved.
body.impact: rehearse-cold is documented and briefed as the cheap, token-free pre-flight, so target repos are told to run it constantly and cannot. A fail-fast now names the limitation instead of leading callers through four escalating validator errors, but the capability itself is still loom-only. Generalizing it means a gitignore-aware snapshot walk (or manifest-declared ignore roots) and a graph-derived surface root, both of which move release-plane trust boundaries and need their own tests.

body.evidence: ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER CLAIM, NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY THE RECORDING AGENT. The cited line ranges are individually accurate, but the conclusion ('the registered Deriver seam... produces deterministic structural and scan changes via a single derivation path, with no second/parallel derivation path') is false for the scan half of the claim. ScanDeriver::derive() (src/seed.rs:470-481, wraps crate::scan::run) is never actually invoked anywhere: derivers() (21-23) is only consumed by sync_derivers() (26-31), which filters by runs_on_sync(), and ScanDeriver.runs_on_sync() returns false (467-469) — so sync_derivers() never includes ScanDeriver, confirmed by the file's own test at seed.rs:495-505 (`sync_runs_structural_but_not_the_external_scan`, asserting sync_derivers()==["structural"] only). Repo-wide grep confirms `.derive(` is called exactly once, at sync.rs:187, over that scan-excluding list — so ScanDeriver::derive is unreachable dead code. Meanwhile the real `loom scan run` CLI command (src/commands/diagnostics_cmd.rs:745) calls `crate::scan::run_unlocked(&root, ...)` directly, completely bypassing the Deriver trait/seam. That is a second, parallel derivation path for scan changes that the criterion explicitly claims does not exist.

Serving live tools is distinct from the session handshake and preserves the protocol surface without duplicating impact semantics.

Protocol-versus-tool classification and session continuity are one observable recovery contract across the two failure steps.

The authored step separates an invalid request from a tool execution failure; an unimplemented METHOD is the third class the code already answers with -32601, and an id-less notification is answered not at all, both leaving the session usable.

Citations to src/commands/hook_cmd.rs (12-26 SYNC_HOOKS/MARKER/loom_owned, 93-98 refuse-before-write, line 17 SYNC_CONTENT fail-open, 123-135 Remove gated by loom_owned) are all accurate as quoted. But intent_desc makes a universal claim: managed hooks touch ONLY Loom-owned post-commit and post-merge hooks. That's false on this same file: `const PRE_PUSH_HOOK: &str = "pre-push"` (line 13) is actively managed. In HookCmd::Install (lines 72-90), when `pre_push` is Some, `targets` becomes `vec![(PRE_PUSH_HOOK, pre_push_content(script)?)]` (line 85) -- installing a pre-push hook INSTEAD OF the sync hooks, not in addition -- and pre_push_content (lines 28-44) builds a blocking 'local CI gate' hook, distinct from the fail-open sync hook. In HookCmd::Remove (line 126), `for name in SYNC_HOOKS.iter().copied().chain([PRE_PUSH_HOOK])` explicitly also considers the pre-push hook. The proposed_criterion silently patches this by inserting '(and pre-push CI)' into its own restatement, which intent_desc itself never says -- exactly the kind of quiet narrowing/widening the review is meant to catch. As literally stated, intent_desc's 'only Loom-owned post-commit and post-merge hooks' is contradicted by the code's own pre-push management.
body.impact: If the claim holds, the implements edge de39b9de is not grounded as asserted and should be re-verdicted. nodes.name: Sub-driver graph writes hand-roll exit-75 retry loops; the CLI could retry pure fact writes internally with bounded jitter
nodes.description: Every parallel-driver integration re-implements the same retry playbook; a missed retry misreads infrastructure contention as a failed write and drops an otherwise-honest verdict

body.evidence: Campaign observation 2026-08-17: 12 coordinated llm:quality sub-drivers recording 480 rule verdicts hit ~10 loom-lock-contention exits (exit 75, ~2% of writes; one worker needed 4 consecutive retries), and every worker independently implemented the same wait-2s-and-retry loop the docs prescribe. The exclusive lock acquisition (src/store/mod.rs, LOCK_WAIT_BUDGET_MS=2000 per loom limits) fails fast by design, but for single-fact write commands (rule verdict, finding verdict, edge verdict) a bounded in-CLI retry with jitter would preserve single-writer semantics while removing per-driver boilerplate
body.impact: Every parallel-driver integration re-implements the same retry playbook; a missed retry misreads infrastructure contention as a failed write and drops an otherwise-honest verdict
